evidence: Cato Agr. praef. 3: mercātōrem autem strēnuum studiōsumque reī quaerendae exīstimō
terms.comment: Especially the wholesale trader who buys in bulk and ships goods, as against the retailer (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Suet. Claud. 18.2: negōtiātōribus certa lucra prōposuit, he offered merchants a sure profit
terms.comment: A wholesale dealer or banker (Lewis & Short); see business.

phrases.latin: luctantem Īcariīs flūctibus Āfricum mercātor metuēns ōtium et oppidī laudat rūra suī; mox reficit ratēs quassās, indocilis pauperiem patī.
phrases.english: The merchant, afraid of the south-west wind wrestling with the Icarian waves, praises a quiet life and the fields of his home town; soon he is refitting his battered ships, unable to learn to put up with being poor.

phrases.latin: Mercātōrem autem strēnuum studiōsumque reī quaerendae exīstimō, vērum, ut suprā dīxī, perīculōsum et calamitōsum.
phrases.english: The merchant I consider energetic and keen to make money, but, as I said above, exposed to danger and disaster.

sources: Lewis & Short: mercator · Lewis & Short: negotiator
